title: A text fallback for spoken answers
statement: Give a spoken-answer task a text fallback of equal status, and keep speech-recognition errors, accent and noise from counting against the content.
detail: The assessment pattern library in the reading project's knowledge base lists speech-recognition errors, accent bias and background noise among what contaminates spoken evidence, citing published evidence of racial disparities in major recognition systems, and asks for a text-response fallback of equal status, noise and accent policies, and retakes when the environment likely interfered (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0158-assessment-pattern-library-brainlift.qmd`). It uses audio features only when fluency is part of the claim. The reading course scores pronunciation leniently, without penalising accent or a noisy room (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0181-vocabulary-rulings.qmd`).
against: The reading course requires a word's say-back to be spoken, with typing not accepted, and records as an unresolved contradiction that a child with no working microphone then has no fallback (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0181-vocabulary-rulings.qmd`). A later run found: The reading course renderer's vocabulary rules record the same gap: learners may speak or type everywhere except the vocabulary say-back, which is spoken regardless, so speech is compulsory for a learner who may have no microphone, and what that task does when speech is unavailable awaits a decision (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/vocabulary.md`, lines 346-358) (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/vocabulary.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/feedback-reconciliation/invariants.dom.txt`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/artifacts/judgment-corpus/distilled-src/04-CONTENT-AUTHORING.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/vocabulary.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/rules/vocabulary.md`).

evidence.quote: Always provide a text-response fallback of equal status
Speech recognition errors, accent bias, and background noise can contaminate evidence.
Evidence of racial disparities in major ASR systems
Audio features (only if fluency is part of the claim): Rate-of-speech, pauses, prosody—do not use for content-only claims.
don't penalize accent or a noisy room
For the vocabulary say-back specifically, require speech. Do not accept typing as a substitute for saying the word.
Where a task needs a microphone or headphones, the child must have a route through without them
This is a confirmed usability trap for a learner who cannot speak; no pronunciation or successful speech observation was obtained.
A child who chooses not to speak should be able to continue before encountering that failure.
Do not mark the word mastered or pretend speech occurred.
typed or equivalent input, silence, denial, error, and no-microphone paths complete the task
a child who says nothing still finishes the lesson.
Spoken and written go to the same marker and the same rubric; the only difference is that a speaker is not marked down for punctuation they never chose.
the vocabulary say-back is spoken regardless (R-VOC-10)
So: choice everywhere, except one task where speech is compulsory, for a child who may have no microphone. Needs a decision on what that task does when speech is unavailable.
The answer is transcribed speech: ignore filler words, missing punctuation, capital letters and small transcription slips. Never mark down spelling.
PASS Capture failure offers honor fallback and is not a scored miss
presence-only capability check, explicit microphone start, non-speaking route reachable before browser speech calls
Say and use each orally or in text. Do not require a microphone to continue.
Tour copy must describe available typing and speech paths; omit stale narration until a matching recording exists.
Infrastructure failure is not learner failure
A child with no microphone, or who says nothing, can still finish every
**R-VOC-10 — say-back must be spoken, not typed**: typing is not accepted as a substitute for the vocabulary say-back specifically, because vocalizing is vital for orthographic encoding
**R-VOC-11 — pronunciation is scored leniently**: anything reasonably correct passes, an accent or noisy room is never penalised, and XP is kept off the pronunciation task
**Rule.** For the vocabulary say-back specifically, require speech. Do not accept typing as a substitute for saying the word.
